title: What's new: Cross-environment Master Data Management
summary: This video covers cross-environment master data management in Business Central 2026 Wave 2. Until now, master data could only be synchronized between companies in the same environment. Now a subsidiary in a different environment of the same tenant can pull data from the headquarters company, using the same mapping, engine and UI as before. The presenters explain the Microsoft Entra app registration, admin consent and permission set that control access. A demo then shows the setup wizard, the initial synchronization, and a customer name change flowing from the source to the subsidiary.

features.name: Cross-environment master data management
features.description: Subsidiaries in the same tenant but in different environments can pull master data from the HQ company. It is built in, with no middleware, no custom code and no extra service, and it uses the same UI and similar setup as same-environment synchronization.
caveats: All environments must be in the same tenant
prerequisites: Same tenant for HQ and subsidiaries

features.name: Pull-based synchronization from read-only HQ
features.description: HQ stays the read-only main source of data. Subsidiaries pull data across the environment boundary and only receive the changes, not everything each time.
caveats: Underlying technology was described as a web service (caption wording uncertain)

features.name: Entra app registration and admin consent
features.description: The company registers an app in Microsoft Entra, and the HQ admin approves it by giving consent in Business Central. The app needs API read/write all application-level permissions, a redirect URL and a single-tenant sign-in audience.
caveats: Details to be documented, according to the presenter
prerequisites: App registered in the same tenant (Azure portal)
Admin consent in the source environment

features.name: Permission set for HQ read access
features.description: When the Entra user for the app is created in the source, the admin assigns a purpose-designed permission set. It includes read permissions for the default tables, so the HQ admin controls who reads what.
caveats: Added tables beyond the default ones need a new permission set with read permissions
prerequisites: Entra user for the app in the source environment

features.name: Pictures and attachments sync
features.description: Pictures and attachments travel along with the synchronized record.
caveats: Pictures limited to 512 KB each for now

features.name: Cross environment setup wizard
features.description: A new action in master data management opens a wizard where the subsidiary consents to the privacy notice and enters the HQ environment name, company name, and the client ID and secret of the app. Credentials are stored securely and cannot be read afterwards.

features.name: Shared or per-subsidiary app registration
features.description: The customer can register one app and share it across several subsidiaries, or register one app for each, depending on their audit requirements.

features.name: Initial synchronization across environments
features.description: The subsidiary starts the initial synchronization with Start all, which runs the default tables in a predefined order, beginning with the business relation table and then dimensions. In the demo, customers, vendors and other default master data arrived in the empty subsidiary.

features.name: Automatic change propagation and synchronization log
features.description: Changes made in the source, such as a customer name, show up in the subsidiary after about a minute. The synchronization tables and log pages work as for single-environment synchronization, and job rescheduling is automatic.
caveats: Change appeared after about a minute
